def.brief: Write tests for Q-review-fixes into test_dwitbuk.py (free functions named test_Q_review_fixes_..., this file's helpers, its own __main__ runner), on real git output where git is involved. (1) Renames in the eyes request: with --since, from a review's base and for a subdirectory target — git mv src.py reviews/src.py shows src.py's deletion and nothing of reviews/src.py; an ordinary rename shows the old path's deletion and the new file; a record moved to a source path shows the new file without the record's deletion. (2) Batching: with dwitbuk.PATHSPEC_BATCH_BYTES lowered (set it on the module, restore it after), an eyes request over many changed source files diffs every one of them, in git's order, and every git diff call it makes keeps its pathspec arguments within the limit (record the calls by wrapping dwitbuk.git); the diff equals what one unbatched git diff of those paths gives. (3) verify_packet's excluded_diff for an excluded bare hunsu.json, after hunsu.json became a directory holding a tracked child.py, holds nothing of child.py (child.py stays in diff when touched); an excluded entry ending in / still shows its files. (4) An untracked nested repository (git init inside, at a declared bare file's name and at an ordinary name) does not crash the eyes request and is not in new_files. (5) Q-hostcall: for both eyes_worker adapters, the child's env equals the parent's minus exactly the six identity/metadata keys, with AGENT_HOST/AGENT_WORKER set (and CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1 for claude), including HOME, LANG, an XDG_*, an SSH_*, a CLAUDE_CODE_* and an arbitrary marker key. (1), (2), (3) and (4) fail on the current tree; (5) passes on the vendored hostcall.py, so show it failing against a copy outside the repository whose worker_env passes only an allow-list. Red evidence is the real suite or focused python3 -c runs, never python3 -m unittest; no mutation campaign. Change no repository file but test_dwitbuk.py; do not commit.

non-claims: no check decides this task; done means the agent said so

(provider) test_session_start_hook_says_what_the_placed_reviews_still_need_and_nothing_else already failed before my change, and the cause is this environment: the session sets AGENT_WORKER=1, so the hook steps aside. It passes with `env -u AGENT_WORKER`. The check `python3 test_dwitbuk.py` will keep failing here for that reason alone, whatever the build does.
(provider) "default well under the platform's argument limit" is tested as 1024 <= PATHSPEC_BATCH_BYTES <= 262144. That range is my reading of 'well under', not a number the contract gives.

(provider) "each git call's pathspec arguments together stay within" is measured as the summed UTF-8 bytes of every argument after `--` in each recorded git diff call, :(literal) prefix included. Separators and the environment are not counted. git calls made outside dwitbuk.git are not seen.

(provider) "The request may stop calling git once the diff has passed its 80000-character cut" is permissive, so no test requires it. The over-ARG_MAX test only checks that the request completes, that diff_truncated is true, and that the diff starts at git's first path.
(provider) "candidate listing": only the packet's diff and new_files are checked. No test reads an intermediate candidate list.

(provider) The test that the batched diff equals one call's output was checked only for a target at the repository root. Under a subdirectory target the diff header prefix is not pinned. The rename tests strip a leading 'proj/' when it is there.
(provider) "a record moved to a source path shows the new file": with git mv the new file is staged, so it is checked in the diff (new file mode), not in new_files.
(provider) Findings 5, 7 and 9, which the section says are "not changed in this run", have no tests.

response.summary:
Added 14 tests named test_Q_review_fixes_* to test_dwitbuk.py. They are free functions that use the file's own helpers (Project, git, run, late_packet, strict_project, hostcall_call) and run under its own __main__ runner. Everything runs on real git output.

Red evidence from the real suite (`python3 test_dwitbuk.py`), failures by part:
- (1) Renames, 3 tests (latest-review base, --since, a target inside a larger repository): all fail. With git mv the diff has no deletion of src.py or old.py, because git's default rename detection keeps only the new names.
- (2) Batching, 3 tests: all fail. The first two fail because dwitbuk.PATHSPEC_BATCH_BYTES is missing. The third, 1400 changed files whose names add up to more than macOS ARG_MAX (1048576), fails with OSError [Errno 7] Argument list too long. The main batching test lowers the limit to 200, records every call through dwitbuk.git, and checks four things: every git diff call keeps its pathspec arguments within the limit; there are at least three content batches; the files come in git's listed order; the diff equals one unbatched `git diff --no-renames`.
- (3) excluded_diff, 2 tests: the bare-entry test fails because excluded_diff for bare hunsu.json and custom-record.json still holds their child.py diffs. The other test checks that an `alpha/` entry shows its files and that a bare file entry shows only itself.
- (4) Nested repositories, 2 tests (one at an ordinary name, one at hunsu.json and custom-record.json): both fail with IsADirectoryError.
- (5) Hostcall, 2 tests: these pass on the vendored hostcall.py. Against a copy outside the repository whose worker_env passes only an allow-list, both failed: HOME was missing for claude and for codex. The 9 earlier Q_hostcall tests still passed on that copy, so these new tests are what catch it.

I checked the helpers on hand-built `git diff --no-renames` output: the correct diff passes the rename checks, and a diff that includes the record's deletion is caught. Only test_dwitbuk.py changed; nothing was committed.
